metadata.case_name: VALLANCE SIMON NEIL v. LAI SZE FUNG

plaintiff.occupation_before: manager at a bar (Murphy's Irish Pub)
plaintiff.occupation_after: worked briefly as manager at Whisky Priest; then worked at a motorbike shop; started his own business in around February 2004

injuries.description: fracture of medial plateau of left proximal tibia
source: (a) fracture of medial plateau of left proximal tibia;

(c) the Plaintiff was still left with residual irregularity of the joint surface (malunion). This was the cause of the persistent pain in his left knee. The significant muscle wasting of his left thigh was good evidence that his complaint of persistent pain in his left knee was a genuine one;
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of upper end of tibia, medial condyle

injuries.description: rupture of ulnar collateral ligament of right 1st metacarpophalangeal joint
source: (b) rupture of ulnar collateral ligament of right 1st metacarpophalangeal joint;

(d) the Plaintiff was still left with residual discomfort and swelling of the 1st matacarpophalangeal joint. Physical examination revealed soft tissue swelling of the capsule and the ligament of the joint. The pain is associated with radially directed force to the joint. There is also mild limitation of the movement of the joint;
injuries.icd_description: Traumatic rupture of collateral ligament of finger at metacarpophalangeal or interphalangeal joint

injuries.description: avulsion fracture of lateral condyle of right 1st metatarsal
injuries.body_part: right 1st metatarsal / right big toe (MTP joint)
source: (c) avulsion fracture of lateral condyle of right 1st metatarsal;

(e) the Plaintiff has residual pain and swelling at the basal joint of his right big toe. There was bony swelling of the joint with limitation and pain with dorsiflexion of his right big toe. X-ray shown permanent abnormality of the joint with malunion of the fracture and there were signs of degenerative arthritics of the 1st metatarsal-phalangeal joint of his right foot. The pain in his right big toe was the cause of the limitation for full squatting;

injuries.description: fracture of proximal phalanx of left 4th toe
source: (d) fracture of proximal phalanx of left 4th toe;
(f) the Plaintiff had recovered well from the fracture of the proximal phalanx of his left 4th toe, and from the injury of his left hip and abdomen;

manifestations.description: Pain in left knee (not persistent in nature) associated with getting out of bed in the morning, after walking for more than 30 minutes, getting up from the seat after sitting for more than 45 minutes, climbing stairs, kneeling on the left knee, poor weather
Swelling of the MCP joint of his right thumb
Discomfort in the MCP joint of his right thumb with poor weather and using tools such as spanner, screw driver and hammer
Bony swelling over the knuckle of his right big toe
Pain in his right big toe with full squatting, wearing tighter shoes and starting the vintage motorcycle
Frequent ache in his back and neck after the accident, usually occurring at the end of the working hours

treatments_received: arthroscopically assisted close reduction and screw fixation
left knee and the right thumb were braced
ankle walker given to his right foot
physiotherapy as an outpatient up to about 2002
treatments_future: total joint replacement of left knee (considered if pain becomes significant; chance estimated by Dr. Lau at about 30%)
fusion of the MTP joint of right big toe (accepted as reasonable and awarded)
replacement of the MTP joint of right big toe (discussed as an option by Dr. Lau)

losses.description: Plaintiff cannot return to his pre-injury job as a manager of a bar restaurant as this involves a lot of walking including climbing of stairs within the restaurant

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies

losses.description: Residual discomfort, swelling and weakness affecting right 1st metacarpophalangeal joint resulting in reduced hand grip
